subject: social_science
chapter_title: The Parliamentary System: Legislature and Executive

concepts.title: India's Parliamentary System
concepts.definition: India follows a parliamentary form of government in which the executive is drawn from and answerable to the legislature; the Constituent Assembly debates of 1949 chose this model so that elected representatives directly control the government of the day.
concepts.key_idea: The government sits in the legislature and answers to it - the heart of parliamentary democracy.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees106.txt lines 1-76 (constitutional choice, Constituent Assembly debates)
question_patterns: what is a parliamentary system of government
why did India choose the parliamentary model
how is the government formed in a parliamentary system
what does collective responsibility mean
compare the parliamentary and presidential systems
why must ministers be members of parliament

solution_steps.explain: Ministers are chosen from among members of parliament.
The council of ministers must keep the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
The 1949 Assembly debates show why India adopted this responsible model.

concepts.title: The Legislature: Parliament and Its Functions
concepts.definition: Parliament - the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha with the President - is the legislature that makes laws, controls finances, questions the government and represents the people; its legislative functions follow a bill's journey from introduction to presidential assent.
concepts.key_idea: Parliament debates, makes laws and holds the government to account on the people's behalf.
question_patterns: name the two houses of the Indian parliament
what are the main functions of the legislature
how does a bill become a law in India
what is the difference between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha
how does parliament control the executive
describe the legislative procedure in parliament

solution_steps.explain: Elected Lok Sabha and mostly elected Rajya Sabha together form Parliament.
Bills pass through readings and votes in both houses before presidential assent.

solution_steps.action: watch the purse and the government
solution_steps.explain: Budget approval, questions and motions keep the executive answerable.

concepts.title: The Executive: President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
concepts.definition: The executive runs the government: the President is the constitutional head who acts on advice, while the Prime Minister and the council of ministers take real decisions; the Vice President presides over the Rajya Sabha, and ministers answer for their departments.
concepts.key_idea: Nominal head in the President, real power with the Prime Minister and ministers.
question_patterns: who is the head of the Indian state and what are the powers of the office
how is the Prime Minister appointed
what is the role of the council of ministers
why does the Vice President preside over the Rajya Sabha
distinguish the nominal executive from the real executive
what are the functions of the President of India

solution_steps.explain: Elected indirectly, the President appoints the Prime Minister and acts on ministerial advice.
The Prime Minister leads the majority party's ministers who run departments.
Ministers answer to parliament and hold office while confidence lasts.

concepts.title: Rights, Duties and the Working of Democracy
concepts.definition: The parliamentary system works inside constitutional limits: the legislature and executive must uphold fundamental rights and follow the directive principles while making policy, keeping governance bound to justice, liberty and equality for all citizens.
concepts.key_idea: Power flows within constitutional rails - rights and principles guide both parliament and government.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees106.txt lines 290-347 (upholding fundamental rights and directive principles)
question_patterns: how do fundamental rights limit the parliament and the executive
what are directive principles of state policy
why must laws respect fundamental rights
give an example of a law guided by directive principles
how does the constitution check the power of the government
what happens when a law violates fundamental rights

solution_steps.explain: No law or executive act may violate fundamental rights.
Directive principles guide policy toward social and economic justice.
Courts review, parliament legislates and the executive implements within these bounds.
